defs.def: an underground railway/railroad system in a city 地下铁道；地铁交通

ex.s: The Barcelona subway pulls into the station, the doors slide open and passengers pour out to go about their daily business.
ex.t: 巴塞罗那地铁驶入车站，车门滑开，乘客们鱼贯而出，各自忙碌日常事务。

ex.s: Bernardo Espinoza, an engineer who takes the subway every day, owns an electric car.
ex.t: 每天乘地铁的工程师Bernardo Espinoza拥有一辆电动汽车。

ex.s: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
ex.t: “我感到惊喜，因为我总是在找哪里能给它充电，”Espinoza在巴塞罗那南部一个工薪阶层社区乘地铁前说。

defs.def: a path that goes under a road, etc. which people can use to cross to the other side （穿越马路等的）地下人行道

ex.s: He found inspiration where others could not, in simple, everyday scenes, such as a man buying oranges at the local grocery store, or a woman riding home on the graffiti-covered subway.
ex.t: 他在别人难以发现的地方——平凡的日常场景中——找到了灵感，比如一个在当地杂货店买橘子的男人，或一位乘坐涂满涂鸦的地铁回家的女人。

ex.s: New Yorkers used to see the graffiti on the walls of poor neighbourhoods and subway trains as something threatening and as an example of urban decay.
ex.t: 纽约人过去常把贫民区墙壁和地铁列车上的涂鸦视为一种威胁，是城市衰败的表现。

ex.s: Later, the image of graffiti and graffiti artists changed a lot and graffiti was no longer only found in the subways and the poor areas of cities.
ex.t: 后来，涂鸦和涂鸦艺术家的形象大为改观，涂鸦不再只出现在地铁和城市贫困地区。

ex.s: Ah Interesting 4 -The American "subway" is called the"underground" in the UK, or the "tube" in London.
ex.t: 啊，有意思 4 ——美国的“subway”在英国叫“underground”，在伦敦叫“tube”。

ex.t: 我们决定留在伦敦，觉得住在2市中心会很棒，这样我们可以轻松步行到各处，也不用在昂贵的3地铁票上花钱。
